records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהֹוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,

records.heading: Pharaoh chases Israel

records.source: דַּבֵּר֮ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וְיָשֻׁ֗בוּ וְיַחֲנוּ֙ לִפְנֵי֙ פִּ֣י הַחִירֹ֔ת בֵּ֥ין מִגְדֹּ֖ל וּבֵ֣ין הַיָּ֑ם לִפְנֵי֙ בַּ֣עַל צְפֹ֔ן נִכְח֥וֹ תַחֲנ֖וּ עַל־הַיָּֽם׃
records.gloss: Speak to [the] sons of Israel, that they turn back and camp before Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and between the sea; before Baal-zephon, opposite it, you will camp by the sea.
pieces: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to turn around and set up camp in front of Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea. Make your camp beside the sea, across from Baal-zephon.

L.2: "Speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, that they turn back and camp before Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea; before Baal-zephon, opposite it, you will camp by the sea.

R.2: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to go back and camp near a place called Pi-hahiroth. It is between Migdol and the sea. Have them camp by the sea, across from Baal-zephon.

decisions.choice: Pi-hahiroth, Migdol, Baal-zephon: places near the sea whose sites are not known for certain
decisions.reason: These names marked Israel's camp beside the sea (verse 9; Numbers 33:7-8). "Migdol" means "tower" or "fort", and Baal-zephon carries the name of the god Baal. None of the three places can be located with certainty today, so the exact route and the place of the crossing cannot be fixed from these names.

decisions.choice: turn back: a change of direction that God orders on purpose
decisions.reason: Israel had camped at the edge of the wilderness (13:20). Turning back puts them where they look trapped between the wilderness and the sea, and verses 3-4 give God's reason: to draw Pharaoh out after them.

decisions.choice: Make your camp ... / Have them camp ...
decisions.reason: The Hebrew changes from "they" to "you" (plural) in the last clause. Balanced keeps the direct command; Readable keeps it as part of what Moses is to tell the people.

records.source: וְאָמַ֤ר פַּרְעֹה֙ לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נְבֻכִ֥ים הֵ֖ם בָּאָ֑רֶץ סָגַ֥ר עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם הַמִּדְבָּֽר׃
records.gloss: And will say Pharaoh of [the] sons of Israel, wandering in confusion [are] they in the land; has shut on them the wilderness.
pieces: Pharaoh will say about the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, 'They are lost and wandering about the country; the wilderness has trapped them.'

L.3: And Pharaoh will say of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, 'They [are] wandering in confusion in the land; the wilderness has closed [the way] on them.'

R.3: Pharaoh will tell himself, 'The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} are lost. They are wandering around, and the desert has them trapped.'

decisions.choice: wandering in confusion: lost, not knowing which way to go
decisions.reason: The verb describes people who are confused and at a loss (Joel 1:18 uses it of cattle with no pasture; Esther 3:15 of a city in dismay). Pharaoh will think Israel has lost its way.

decisions.choice: the wilderness has shut them in: they are trapped
decisions.reason: With the wilderness behind them and the sea in front, Israel would look boxed in, an easy target for an army.

decisions.choice: will tell himself
decisions.reason: "Say" here is what Pharaoh will say or think about Israel, not words spoken to them. Readable makes that plain.

records.source: וְחִזַּקְתִּ֣י אֶת־לֵב־פַּרְעֹה֮ וְרָדַ֣ף אַחֲרֵיהֶם֒ וְאִכָּבְדָ֤ה בְּפַרְעֹה֙ וּבְכָל־חֵיל֔וֹ וְיָדְע֥וּ מִצְרַ֖יִם כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־כֵֽן׃
records.gloss: And I will make strong [the] heart of Pharaoh, and he will pursue after them, and I will get glory by Pharaoh and by all his army, and will know Egypt that I [am] Yahweh. And they did so.
pieces: I will make Pharaoh's heart stubborn, and he will chase after them. Then I will win glory at the expense of Pharaoh and all his forces, and the Egyptians will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." The Israelites did as they were told.

L.4: And I will make the heart of Pharaoh strong, and he will pursue after them, and I will get glory over Pharaoh and over all his army, and the Egyptians will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." And they did so.

R.4: I will make Pharaoh stubborn, and he will chase after them. But I will defeat Pharaoh and his whole army, and that will bring {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} glory. Then the Egyptians will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." So the Israelites did what they were told.

decisions.choice: I will make Pharaoh's heart strong: God confirms Pharaoh in his resistance
decisions.reason: The verb means to make firm or strong, as in 4:21 and 11:10. See the note at 7:3.

decisions.choice: I will get glory: be honored, show my weight
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the root "heavy", the root of Pharaoh's "heavy" heart (7:14; 9:7). Pharaoh made his heart heavy against God; now God will be "heavy", that is honored and glorious, through Pharaoh's defeat. The same verb returns in verses 17-18, and the root again in verse 25.

decisions.choice: the Egyptians will know that I am Yahweh: the purpose of the plagues reaches its end
decisions.reason: God said in 7:5 that the Egyptians would know that he is Yahweh when he brought Israel out. Pharaoh had asked, "Who is Yahweh?" (5:2).

decisions.choice: The Israelites
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "they did so"; Balanced and Readable name the Israelites.

decisions.choice: I will defeat Pharaoh ... and that will bring me glory
decisions.reason: Readable says how God will win glory over Pharaoh: by defeating him, as the rest of the chapter tells.

records.source: וַיֻּגַּד֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם כִּ֥י בָרַ֖ח הָעָ֑ם וַ֠יֵּהָפֵךְ לְבַ֨ב פַּרְעֹ֤ה וַעֲבָדָיו֙ אֶל־הָעָ֔ם וַיֹּֽאמרוּ֙ מַה־זֹּ֣את עָשִׂ֔ינוּ כִּֽי־שִׁלַּ֥חְנוּ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵעָבְדֵֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: And it was told to [the] king of Egypt that had fled the people, and was turned [the] heart of Pharaoh and his servants toward the people, and they said, what [is] this we have done, that we have let go Israel from serving us?
pieces: Word reached the king of Egypt that the people had run away, and Pharaoh and his officials turned against them. "Why did we do this?" they said. "We have let Israel go, and they will no longer serve us!"

L.5: And it was told to the king of Egypt that the people had fled, and the heart of Pharaoh and his servants was turned against the people, and they said, "What [is] this we have done, that we have let Israel go from serving us?"

R.5: Someone told the king of Egypt that the Israelites had run away. Then Pharaoh and his officials turned against them. They said, "Why did we do this? We let the Israelites go, and now we have lost our slaves!"

decisions.choice: fled: gone for good
decisions.reason: Pharaoh had sent Israel out (12:31-32), and earlier the request had been for a journey of three days to worship (5:3). The report that the people have "fled" means that they are not coming back.

decisions.choice: the heart was turned: they changed their minds
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought and will. Their heart toward the people "turned": they regretted letting Israel go and turned against them.

decisions.choice: let Israel go from serving us: released them, so they no longer serve us
decisions.reason: Pharaoh's loss is a loss of labor. The word "serve" is the one God used: Israel was to go "that they may serve me" (9:1).

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: Pharaoh's "servants" are his court and officials (5:21; 11:3). Balanced and Readable say "officials"; Literal keeps "servants".

decisions.choice: our slaves
decisions.reason: "Slaves" in Readable, as the style guide keeps it for Israel's slavery in Egypt: Egypt has lost the people it held in bondage.

records.source: וַיֶּאְסֹ֖ר אֶת־רִכְבּ֑וֹ וְאֶת־עַמּ֖וֹ לָקַ֥ח עִמּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And he harnessed his chariot, and his people he took with him.
pieces: Then Pharaoh had his chariot harnessed and took his troops along.

L.6: And he harnessed his chariot and took his people with him.

R.6: So Pharaoh had his war chariot hitched up, and he gathered his army to go with him.

decisions.choice: his people: his fighting men, his army
decisions.reason: "People" here means the men under arms, as in Numbers 20:20, where Edom comes out with "many people".

decisions.choice: he harnessed: he had it harnessed
decisions.reason: A king gives the order; the verb says what was done at his command.

decisions.choice: Pharaoh
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "he"; Balanced and Readable name Pharaoh.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֗ח שֵׁשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת רֶ֨כֶב֙ בָּח֔וּר וְכֹ֖ל רֶ֣כֶב מִצְרָ֑יִם וְשָׁלִשִׁ֖ם עַל־כֻּלּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And he took six hundred chariots chosen, and all [the] chariotry of Egypt, and officers over all of it.
pieces: He took 600 picked chariots and the rest of Egypt's chariot force too, with officers over the whole of it.

L.7: And he took 600 chosen chariots, and all the chariotry of Egypt, and officers over all of it.

R.7: He took his 600 best chariots. He also took every other chariot in Egypt. Officers were in charge of all of them.

decisions.choice: officers: high-ranking soldiers in the chariot force
alternatives: third men (a third man in each chariot)
decisions.reason: The word is related to the word for "three". It may name the third man in a chariot, beside the driver and the fighter, or an officer of high rank (2 Kings 9:25; 10:25). Either way, the chariots went out with their commanders.

decisions.choice: all the chariotry of Egypt: the rest of the chariots, besides the 600 chosen ones
decisions.reason: The 600 picked chariots led the way, and the rest of Egypt's chariots went with them. Chariots were light, horse-drawn vehicles for war, the fastest and strongest part of Egypt's army.

records.source: וַיְחַזֵּ֣ק יְהֹוָ֗ה אֶת־לֵ֤ב פַּרְעֹה֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיִּרְדֹּ֕ף אַחֲרֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יֹצְאִ֖ים בְּיָ֥ד רָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And made strong Yahweh [the] heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursued after [the] sons of Israel, and [the] sons of Israel [were] going out with a hand high.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} made the heart of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, stubborn, and he went after the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, who were leaving with heads held high.

L.8: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt strong, and he pursued after the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel were going out with a high hand.

R.8: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} made Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, stubborn. So Pharaoh chased the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, who were leaving boldly.

decisions.choice: Yahweh made Pharaoh's heart strong: as God said in verse 4
decisions.reason: See the note at 7:3.

decisions.choice: with a high hand: boldly, openly
alternatives: under the power of God's raised hand
decisions.reason: A raised hand is a sign of strength and confidence. Israel left in the open, without fear (Numbers 33:3 says the same of the night they left, "in the sight of all the Egyptians"). The phrase may also point to God's power: the raised hand would then be the hand of God that brought them out (6:1; 13:9). In Numbers 15:30 the same phrase means "defiantly".

decisions.choice: with heads held high (Balanced); boldly (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses an English picture of confidence for the Hebrew one; Readable says what it means. Literal keeps "with a high hand".

records.source: וַיִּרְדְּפ֨וּ מִצְרַ֜יִם אַחֲרֵיהֶ֗ם וַיַּשִּׂ֤יגוּ אוֹתָם֙ חֹנִ֣ים עַל־הַיָּ֔ם כָּל־סוּס֙ רֶ֣כֶב פַּרְעֹ֔ה וּפָרָשָׁ֖יו וְחֵיל֑וֹ עַל־פִּי֙ הַֽחִירֹ֔ת לִפְנֵ֖י בַּ֥עַל צְפֹֽן׃
records.gloss: And pursued Egypt after them and overtook them camping by the sea, every horse of [the] chariotry of Pharaoh and his horsemen and his army, beside Pi-hahiroth, before Baal-zephon.
pieces: The Egyptians, all Pharaoh's chariot horses, his horsemen and his army, went after them and caught up with them where they were camped by the sea, beside Pi-hahiroth, facing Baal-zephon.

L.9: And the Egyptians pursued after them and overtook them camping by the sea, every horse of Pharaoh's chariotry and his horsemen and his army, beside Pi-hahiroth, before Baal-zephon.

R.9: The Egyptians chased after the Israelites with all of Pharaoh's chariot horses, his horsemen, and his army. They caught up with the Israelites while they were camped by the sea near Pi-hahiroth, across from Baal-zephon.

decisions.choice: horsemen: the men who drove and fought from the chariots, or riders on horseback
decisions.reason: The word can mean riders, or the horses themselves, or the crews of chariots. Egypt's army at this time fought mainly from chariots, so the "horsemen" may be the chariot crews.

decisions.choice: every horse of Pharaoh's chariotry ...: the list says who "Egypt" was
decisions.reason: The list of horses, horsemen and army stands after the verbs and spells out the force that pursued Israel.

decisions.choice: the Egyptians
decisions.reason: "Egypt" here is the Egyptian army, as often in this chapter, so every level says "the Egyptians".

records.source: וּפַרְעֹ֖ה הִקְרִ֑יב וַיִּשְׂאוּ֩ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל אֶת־עֵינֵיהֶ֜ם וְהִנֵּ֥ה מִצְרַ֣יִם׀נֹסֵ֣עַ אַחֲרֵיהֶ֗ם וַיִּֽירְאוּ֙ מְאֹ֔ד וַיִּצְעֲק֥וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And Pharaoh drew near, and lifted up [the] sons of Israel their eyes, and look, Egypt [was] marching after them, and they feared greatly, and cried out [the] sons of Israel to Yahweh.
pieces: Pharaoh was drawing closer. When the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} looked up, they saw the Egyptians advancing behind them, and they were filled with fear. The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.10: And Pharaoh drew near, and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel lifted up their eyes, and look, the Egyptians [were] marching after them, and they feared greatly, and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.10: Pharaoh and his army came closer. The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} looked up and saw the Egyptians coming after them. They were very afraid, and they cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help.

decisions.choice: cried out: the cry of people in distress
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the Israelites crying out under their slave drivers (5:8, 15), and its noun is the "cry" God heard in 3:7, 9. It is a call for help.

decisions.choice: lifted up their eyes: looked up and saw
decisions.reason: The phrase introduces what someone sees (Genesis 22:4, 13).

decisions.choice: Pharaoh and his army ... for help
decisions.reason: Readable says that Pharaoh came with his army (verse 9) and that the cry was a call for help.

records.source: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֮ אֶל־מֹשֶׁה֒ הַֽמִבְּלִ֤י אֵין־קְבָרִים֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם לְקַחְתָּ֖נוּ לָמ֣וּת בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר מַה־זֹּאת֙ עָשִׂ֣יתָ לָּ֔נוּ לְהוֹצִיאָ֖נוּ מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And they said to Moses, [is it] from there being no graves in Egypt [that] you have taken us to die in the wilderness? What [is] this you have done to us, to bring us out from Egypt?
pieces: They said to Moses, "Did Egypt have no graves, that you had to bring us out here to die in the wilderness? What a thing to do to us, leading us out of Egypt!

L.11: And they said to Moses, "Is it because there are no graves in Egypt [that] you have taken us to die in the wilderness? What [is] this you have done to us, to bring us out of Egypt?

R.11: They said to Moses, "Why did you bring us out here to die in the desert? Were there not enough graves for us in Egypt? Look at what you have done to us by taking us out of Egypt!

decisions.choice: are there no graves in Egypt?: a bitter, mocking question
decisions.reason: The question is ironic. Egypt was famous for its tombs, and the people say they might as well have died and been buried there as die unburied in the wilderness.

decisions.choice: what is this you have done to us?: a reproach
decisions.reason: The question blames Moses. It echoes Pharaoh's own question in verse 5: both sides now regret the exodus.

decisions.choice: two questions in reverse order
decisions.reason: Readable puts the plain complaint first and the ironic question second, so the irony is easier to follow.

records.source: הֲלֹא־זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁר֩ דִּבַּ֨רְנוּ אֵלֶ֤יךָ בְמִצְרַ֨יִם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר חֲדַ֥ל מִמֶּ֖נּוּ וְנַֽעַבְדָ֣ה אֶת־מִצְרָ֑יִם כִּ֣י ט֥וֹב לָ֨נוּ֙ עֲבֹ֣ד אֶת־מִצְרַ֔יִם מִמֻּתֵ֖נוּ בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃
records.gloss: [Is] not this the word which we spoke to you in Egypt, saying, cease from us, that we may serve Egypt? For [it is] good for us to serve Egypt more than our dying in the wilderness.
pieces: Did we not tell you this very thing back in Egypt? We said, 'Let us be, and we will serve the Egyptians.' Serving the Egyptians was better for us than dying here in the wilderness!"

L.12: [Is] not this the word that we spoke to you in Egypt, saying, 'Leave us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians'? For better for us [is] serving the Egyptians than our dying in the wilderness."

R.12: Back in Egypt we told you, 'Leave us alone! Let us go on working for the Egyptians.' Working as slaves for the Egyptians would be better than dying out here in the desert!"

decisions.choice: the word we spoke to you in Egypt: their earlier complaints
decisions.reason: These words are not recorded earlier, but the people's earlier response is: the foremen blamed Moses and Aaron (5:21), and the people would not listen to Moses because of their hard labor (6:9).

decisions.choice: serve the Egyptians: work as their slaves
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used throughout Exodus for serving God (9:1). Under threat, the people would rather serve Egypt than go free to serve God.

decisions.choice: working for / working as slaves for
decisions.reason: Readable says what serving Egypt meant; Literal and Balanced keep "serve", the word used for serving God. "Slaves" stays, as the style guide keeps it for Israel's slavery in Egypt.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֣ה אֶל־הָעָם֮ אַל־תִּירָאוּ֒ הִֽתְיַצְב֗וּ וּרְאוּ֙ אֶת־יְשׁוּעַ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם הַיּ֑וֹם כִּ֗י אֲשֶׁ֨ר רְאִיתֶ֤ם אֶת־מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ הַיּ֔וֹם לֹ֥א תֹסִ֛יפוּ לִרְאֹתָ֥ם ע֖וֹד עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: And said Moses to the people, do not fear. Station yourselves and see [the] salvation of Yahweh, which he will do for you today; for [the] Egypt which you have seen today, not you will again see them any more until forever.
pieces: But Moses told the people, "Have no fear! Hold your ground and watch how {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will save you today. You see the Egyptians today, but you will never see them again.

L.13: And Moses said to the people, "Do not fear. Station yourselves and see the salvation of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will do for you today; for the Egyptians whom you have seen today, you will not see them again any more, forever.

R.13: Moses said to the people, "Do not be afraid. Stay where you are, and you will see {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rescue you today. You will never see these Egyptians again.

decisions.choice: the salvation of Yahweh: Yahweh's rescue from danger
decisions.reason: The noun means rescue or deliverance, help that saves people from a threat they cannot escape. It comes from the verb "save" in verse 30, where the rescue is done. Israel will sing, "He has become my salvation" (15:2).

decisions.choice: station yourselves: stand firm, hold your position
decisions.reason: The verb means to take one's stand and stay there. The people are not to run or fight but to stand and watch what God does.

decisions.choice: you will not see them again: never again as a threat
decisions.reason: The emphatic "not ... again ... forever" promises an end to the danger. Israel does see the Egyptians once more, dead on the shore (verse 30).

decisions.choice: watch how the LORD will save you (Balanced); see the LORD rescue you (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the noun into a verb, with God as its subject. Balanced keeps the word family of "salvation" ("save"); Readable says "rescue", the plain sense. Literal keeps "the salvation of the LORD".

records.source: יְהוָ֖ה יִלָּחֵ֣ם לָכֶ֑ם וְאַתֶּ֖ם תַּחֲרִישֽׁוּן׃פ
records.gloss: Yahweh will fight for you, and you, you will keep silent.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will fight on your behalf, and you can stay quiet."

L.14: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will fight for you, and you, you will keep silent."

R.14: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will fight for you. All you have to do is stay calm."

decisions.choice: Yahweh will fight for you: God as the warrior who defends his people
decisions.reason: Israel will not fight; Yahweh will. In verse 25 the Egyptians themselves say it, and Israel sings, "Yahweh is a man of war" (15:3).

decisions.choice: keep silent: be still, do nothing
decisions.reason: The verb means to be quiet. Set against "Yahweh will fight", it means to stop crying out and complaining and to leave the battle to God.

decisions.choice: stay calm
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of keeping silent here: not panicking, waiting for God to act.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה מַה־תִּצְעַ֖ק אֵלָ֑י דַּבֵּ֥ר אֶל־בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְיִסָּֽעוּ׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, why do you cry out to me? Speak to [the] sons of Israel, that they set out.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Why are you crying out to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to break camp and go forward.

L.15: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Why do you cry out to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? Speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, that they set out.

R.15: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Why are you calling to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for help? Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to start moving.

decisions.choice: why do you cry out to me?: the time for prayer has given way to action
alternatives: Moses had cried out on the people's behalf
decisions.reason: Moses' own cry is not recorded. He may have cried out with the people (verse 10), or he may be addressed as their leader, speaking for them. God's question is not a rebuke of prayer but a call to move.

decisions.choice: set out: break camp and move on
decisions.reason: The verb means to pull up the tent pegs and travel on, as at each stage of the journey (12:37; 13:20).

decisions.choice: break camp and go forward
decisions.reason: Balanced spells out the two parts of the verb: leaving the camp and moving on toward the sea.

records.heading: Crossing the sea on dry ground

records.source: וְאַתָּ֞ה הָרֵ֣ם אֶֽת־מַטְּךָ֗ וּנְטֵ֧ה אֶת־יָדְךָ֛ עַל־הַיָּ֖ם וּבְקָעֵ֑הוּ וְיָבֹ֧אוּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בְּת֥וֹךְ הַיָּ֖ם בַּיַּבָּשָֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And you, raise your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea and split it, that may go [the] sons of Israel in [the] midst of the sea on dry ground.
pieces: As for you, lift up your staff, reach out your hand over the sea, and split it open, so that the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} can walk through the middle of the sea on dry ground.

L.16: And you, raise your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea and split it, that the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel may go into the midst of the sea on dry ground.

R.16: Hold up your staff and reach your hand out over the sea. Split the sea in two, and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} will walk across the middle of it on dry ground.

decisions.choice: split it: divide the sea in two
decisions.reason: The verb means to split or cleave. It is used again of the waters in verse 21 (Psalm 78:13; Nehemiah 9:11).

decisions.choice: dry ground: the word used for the dry land of creation
decisions.reason: The word is the one used when the dry land first appeared from the waters (Genesis 1:9-10). It is used again in verses 22 and 29.

records.source: וַאֲנִ֗י הִנְנִ֤י מְחַזֵּק֙ אֶת־לֵ֣ב מִצְרַ֔יִם וְיָבֹ֖אוּ אַחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם וְאִכָּבְדָ֤ה בְּפַרְעֹה֙ וּבְכָל־חֵיל֔וֹ בְּרִכְבּ֖וֹ וּבְפָרָשָֽׁיו׃
records.gloss: And I, look, I [am] about to make strong [the] heart of Egypt, and they will go after them, and I will get glory by Pharaoh and by all his army, by his chariots and by his horsemen.
pieces: As for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I am going to make the Egyptians stubborn, so that they follow them in. Then I will win glory at the expense of Pharaoh and his whole army, his chariots and his horsemen.

L.17: And I, look, I am about to make the heart of the Egyptians strong, and they will go in after them, and I will get glory over Pharaoh and over all his army, over his chariots and over his horsemen.

R.17: I will make the Egyptians stubborn, and they will follow the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} into the sea. Then I will defeat Pharaoh, his whole army, his chariots, and his horsemen, and that will bring {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} glory.

decisions.choice: I will make the heart of the Egyptians strong: the whole army is now hardened
decisions.reason: Until now God hardened Pharaoh's heart (verses 4, 8). Now the Egyptians as a whole will be made bold enough to follow Israel into the sea. See the note at 7:3.

decisions.choice: I will get glory: as in verse 4
decisions.reason: The verb from the root "heavy" again: God will be honored through the defeat of Pharaoh and his forces. The "heavy" heart (7:14) meets God's weight.

decisions.choice: into the sea ... I will defeat
decisions.reason: Readable says where the Egyptians will follow Israel and how God will win glory, as in verse 4.

records.source: וְיָדְע֥וּ מִצְרַ֖יִם כִּי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה בְּהִכָּבְדִ֣י בְּפַרְעֹ֔ה בְּרִכְבּ֖וֹ וּבְפָרָשָֽׁיו׃
records.gloss: And will know Egypt that I [am] Yahweh, when I get glory by Pharaoh, by his chariots and by his horsemen.
pieces: The Egyptians will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} when I have won glory at the expense of Pharaoh, his chariots, and his horsemen."

L.18: And the Egyptians will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I get glory over Pharaoh, over his chariots, and over his horsemen."

R.18: When I defeat Pharaoh and his chariots and horsemen, it will bring {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} glory. Then the Egyptians will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: the Egyptians will know that I am Yahweh: repeated from verse 4
decisions.reason: The repetition marks the purpose of the whole event (7:5).

decisions.choice: the cause first, then the result
decisions.reason: Readable puts God's victory first and what the Egyptians will learn from it second.

records.source: וַיִּסַּ֞ע מַלְאַ֣ךְ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים הַהֹלֵךְ֙ לִפְנֵי֙ מַחֲנֵ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ מֵאַחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּסַּ֞ע עַמּ֤וּד הֶֽעָנָן֙ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיַּֽעֲמֹ֖ד מֵאַחֲרֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And set out [the] angel of God, the [one] going before [the] camp of Israel, and he went behind them; and set out [the] pillar of the cloud from before them and stood behind them.
pieces: The angel of God, who had been going ahead of Israel's camp, moved and went to the rear, and the pillar of cloud moved from in front of them and took its place behind them.

L.19: And the angel of God, who was going before the camp of Israel, set out and went behind them; and the pillar of cloud set out from before them and stood behind them.

R.19: The angel of God had been leading the Israelites. Now the angel moved and went behind them. The pillar of cloud also moved from the front and stood behind them.

decisions.choice: the angel of God and the pillar of cloud: God's presence guarding Israel
decisions.reason: In 13:21-22 Yahweh went before Israel in the pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire. Here the angel of God and the pillar move together; God himself goes with his people (compare 3:2; 23:20). Now he places himself between them and the enemy.

decisions.choice: the camp of Israel: the whole people on the move
decisions.reason: "Camp" is the people of Israel as a company traveling and camping together. In verse 20 it stands beside "the camp of Egypt", the Egyptian army.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֞א בֵּ֣ין׀מַחֲנֵ֣ה מִצְרַ֗יִם וּבֵין֙ מַחֲנֵ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיְהִ֤י הֶֽעָנָן֙ וְהַחֹ֔שֶׁךְ וַיָּ֖אֶר אֶת־הַלָּ֑יְלָה וְלֹא־קָרַ֥ב זֶ֛ה אֶל־זֶ֖ה כָּל־הַלָּֽיְלָה׃
records.gloss: And it came between [the] camp of Egypt and between [the] camp of Israel; and there was the cloud and the darkness, and it lit up the night, and not came near this to this all the night.
pieces: It came between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel. The cloud was there, and the darkness, and it lit up the night; and all night long neither camp approached the other.

L.20: And it came between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel; and there was the cloud and the darkness, and it lit up the night, and the one did not come near the other all the night.

R.20: It came between the Egyptian camp and the Israelite camp. The cloud brought darkness, and it also gave light in the night. So all night long the two camps did not come near each other.

decisions.choice: the cloud and the darkness, and it lit up the night: the cloud was dark and yet gave light
alternatives: the cloud was dark to the Egyptians and gave light to Israel
and there was darkness and gloom, and the night passed (the Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is very brief and hard to read. The most likely sense is that the same cloud brought darkness and also lit up the night, dark toward the Egyptians and bright toward Israel, so the two camps were kept apart. It may also mean that the pillar of fire (13:21) gave light to Israel while the cloud stood dark. The Greek translation reads differently: "and there was darkness and gloom, and the night passed". The translation keeps the Hebrew and its ambiguity.

decisions.choice: this did not come near this: neither camp came near the other
decisions.reason: "This" and "this" are the two camps named at the start of the verse.

records.source: וַיֵּ֨ט מֹשֶׁ֣ה אֶת־יָדוֹ֮ עַל־הַיָּם֒ וַיּ֣וֹלֶךְ יְהוָ֣ה׀אֶת־הַ֠יָּם בְּר֨וּחַ קָדִ֤ים עַזָּה֙ כָּל־הַלַּ֔יְלָה וַיָּ֥שֶׂם אֶת־הַיָּ֖ם לֶחָרָבָ֑ה וַיִּבָּקְע֖וּ הַמָּֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And stretched out Moses his hand over the sea, and drove Yahweh the sea by a wind, east, strong, all the night, and made the sea into dry land, and were split the waters.
pieces: Moses held his hand out over the sea, and all night long {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} pushed the sea back with a powerful east wind. He turned the sea into dry land, and the waters were split apart.

L.21: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} drove the sea back by a strong east wind all the night, and made the sea into dry land, and the waters were split.

R.21: Moses held his hand out over the sea. All night long {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} pushed the water back with a strong wind from the east. He made the bottom of the sea dry, and the water split apart.

decisions.choice: a strong east wind: the hot wind from the desert
decisions.reason: An east wind blows from the desert and is hot and drying. It brought the locusts in 10:13. Here God uses it to drive back the sea; Israel's song calls it the blast of God's nostrils (15:8).

decisions.choice: drove: made the sea go back
decisions.reason: The verb is the common word "go" in a form meaning "make go". The sea moved back before the wind.

decisions.choice: dry land: ground with the water gone
decisions.reason: This word means land that has been dried out (Genesis 7:22; Joshua 3:17). Verses 16, 22 and 29 use another word, "dry ground". Both describe the seabed laid bare.

decisions.choice: the bottom of the sea
decisions.reason: Readable says which part of the sea became dry.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֧אוּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בְּת֥וֹךְ הַיָּ֖ם בַּיַּבָּשָׁ֑ה וְהַמַּ֤יִם לָהֶם֙ חֹמָ֔ה מִֽימִינָ֖ם וּמִשְּׂמֹאלָֽם׃
records.gloss: And went [the] sons of Israel in [the] midst of the sea on dry ground, and the waters [were] to them a wall on their right and on their left.
pieces: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} went into the middle of the sea on dry ground, and the water was a wall for them, to the right and to the left.

L.22: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel went into the midst of the sea on dry ground, and the waters [were] a wall to them on their right and on their left.

R.22: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} walked through the middle of the sea on dry ground. The water was like a wall on both sides of them, on the right and on the left.

decisions.choice: a wall: a barrier that stood and protected
decisions.reason: A wall is a defense (1 Samuel 25:16, "they were a wall to us"). The waters stood on both sides and kept Israel safe as they crossed. Israel's song says the waters "stood up like a heap" (15:8).

decisions.choice: like a wall
decisions.reason: Readable makes the picture a comparison so that a young reader takes it as a picture of standing water.

records.source: וַיִּרְדְּפ֤וּ מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ אַחֲרֵיהֶ֔ם כֹּ֚ל ס֣וּס פַּרְעֹ֔ה רִכְבּ֖וֹ וּפָרָשָׁ֑יו אֶל־תּ֖וֹךְ הַיָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And pursued Egypt and went after them, every horse of Pharaoh, his chariots and his horsemen, into [the] midst of the sea.
pieces: The Egyptians gave chase and followed them into the middle of the sea, all Pharaoh's horses, his chariots and his horsemen.

L.23: And the Egyptians pursued and went in after them, every horse of Pharaoh, his chariots and his horsemen, into the midst of the sea.

R.23: The Egyptians went after them, right into the middle of the sea. Every one of Pharaoh's horses went in, with his chariots and his horsemen.

decisions.choice: they went after them into the midst of the sea: what God said in verse 17
decisions.reason: God said the Egyptians would go in after Israel (verse 17), and they do. The list of horses, chariots and horsemen again shows the whole force.

records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ בְּאַשְׁמֹ֣רֶת הַבֹּ֔קֶר וַיַּשְׁקֵ֤ף יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מַחֲנֵ֣ה מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּעַמּ֥וּד אֵ֖שׁ וְעָנָ֑ן וַיָּ֕הָם אֵ֖ת מַחֲנֵ֥ה מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And it was in [the] watch of the morning, and looked down Yahweh on [the] camp of Egypt in a pillar of fire and cloud, and he threw into panic [the] camp of Egypt.
pieces: In the last hours of the night, before morning, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} looked down on the Egyptian camp from the pillar of fire and cloud and threw the camp into panic.

L.24: And it was in the morning watch, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} looked down on the camp of Egypt in the pillar of fire and cloud, and threw the camp of Egypt into panic.

R.24: Just before dawn, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} looked down at the Egyptian army from the pillar of fire and cloud. He made the Egyptians panic and fall into confusion.

decisions.choice: the morning watch: the last part of the night, before dawn
decisions.reason: The night was divided into watches, periods when guards kept watch (Judges 7:19; Lamentations 2:19). The morning watch was the last, ending at daybreak. Israel had crossed during the night (verse 21).

decisions.choice: threw into panic: confused and routed
decisions.reason: The verb is used of God throwing an enemy army into confusion and flight (Joshua 10:10; Judges 4:15; 1 Samuel 7:10).

decisions.choice: looked down: looked down from above
decisions.reason: The verb is used of looking down from a height, as God looks down from heaven (Psalm 14:2). From the pillar of fire and cloud, God looked on the Egyptians and acted.

decisions.choice: in the last hours of the night, before morning (Balanced); just before dawn (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "the morning watch" was; Literal keeps the term.

records.source: וַיָּ֗סַר אֵ֚ת אֹפַ֣ן מַרְכְּבֹתָ֔יו וַֽיְנַהֲגֵ֖הוּ בִּכְבֵדֻ֑ת וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מִצְרַ֗יִם אָנ֨וּסָה֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֣י יְהוָ֔ה נִלְחָ֥ם לָהֶ֖ם בְּמִצְרָֽיִם
records.gloss: And he removed [the] wheels of his chariots, and he made it drive with heaviness. And said Egypt, let me flee from before Israel, for Yahweh [is] fighting for them against Egypt.
pieces: He made the wheels come off their chariots, so that they could hardly drive. Then the Egyptians said, "We must run from Israel, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is fighting on their side against Egypt!"

L.25: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} removed the wheels of their chariots and made them drive with heaviness. And the Egyptians said, "Let us flee from before Israel, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is fighting for them against Egypt."

R.25: He made the wheels of their chariots come off, so it was very hard for them to drive. The Egyptians shouted, "Run! Get away from the Israelites! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is fighting for them against Egypt!"

decisions.choice: he removed: the Hebrew text
alternatives: he bound (clogged) the wheels of their chariots
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has "he turned aside", that is, removed or jammed the wheels. The Samaritan Pentateuch and the Greek translation have "he bound", a verb that differs by one letter in Hebrew: the wheels were clogged and stuck. Either way the chariots could not move freely. The translation follows the Hebrew text.

decisions.choice: with heaviness: with difficulty, heavily
decisions.reason: "Heaviness" is from the same root as Pharaoh's "heavy" heart (7:14) and God's "getting glory" (verses 4, 17-18). The army that came out in strength now drags along heavily, and God is honored over it.

decisions.choice: Yahweh is fighting for them: the Egyptians say what Moses said
decisions.reason: Moses told Israel, "Yahweh will fight for you" (verse 14). Now the Egyptians themselves say it, and they begin to know that he is Yahweh (verses 4, 18).

decisions.choice: the Egyptians ... us / we
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "Egypt said, 'Let me flee'", the nation speaking as one person. Every level says "the Egyptians" and "us" or "we".

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה נְטֵ֥ה אֶת־יָדְךָ֖ עַל־הַיָּ֑ם וְיָשֻׁ֤בוּ הַמַּ֨יִם֙ עַל־מִצְרַ֔יִם עַל־רִכְבּ֖וֹ וְעַל־פָּרָשָֽׁיו׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, stretch out your hand over the sea, that may return the waters over Egypt, over his chariots and over his horsemen.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Hold your hand out over the sea, and the waters will flow back over the Egyptians, over their chariots and their horsemen."

L.26: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand over the sea, that the waters may return upon the Egyptians, upon their chariots and upon their horsemen."

R.26: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Hold your hand out over the sea. The water will come back and cover the Egyptians and their chariots and horsemen."

decisions.choice: stretch out your hand over the sea: the same act that opened the sea
decisions.reason: Moses opened the sea by stretching out his hand (verses 16, 21); the same act now closes it.

decisions.choice: that the waters may return: the result God intends
decisions.reason: The verb form states the purpose of the command and what will follow from it.

records.source: וַיֵּט֩ מֹשֶׁ֨ה אֶת־יָד֜וֹ עַל־הַיָּ֗ם וַיָּ֨שָׁב הַיָּ֜ם לִפְנ֥וֹת בֹּ֨קֶר֙ לְאֵ֣יתָנ֔וֹ וּמִצְרַ֖יִם נָסִ֣ים לִקְרָאת֑וֹ וַיְנַעֵ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־מִצְרַ֖יִם בְּת֥וֹךְ הַיָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And stretched out Moses his hand over the sea, and returned the sea at [the] turning of morning to its usual flow, and Egypt [was] fleeing to meet it, and shook off Yahweh Egypt in [the] midst of the sea.
pieces: So Moses held his hand out over the sea, and as morning broke the sea went back to its usual flow. The Egyptians were fleeing straight into it, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} shook them off into the middle of the sea.

L.27: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the sea returned at the turning of morning to its usual flow, and the Egyptians [were] fleeing toward it, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} shook off the Egyptians into the midst of the sea.

R.27: So Moses held out his hand over the sea. As the sun came up, the water flowed back to where it belonged. The Egyptians tried to run away, but they ran right into the water. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} threw them into the middle of the sea.

decisions.choice: its usual flow: its normal, steady state
decisions.reason: The word means what is constant or lasting, like a stream that always flows (Deuteronomy 21:4; Amos 5:24). The sea went back to the way it always was.

decisions.choice: shook off: threw off, as one shakes something off
decisions.reason: The verb is used of shaking something off or out (Judges 16:20; Nehemiah 5:13). Psalm 136:15 uses the same verb of this event: God shook off Pharaoh and his army in the sea.

decisions.choice: fleeing toward it: running into the returning water
decisions.reason: The Egyptians tried to escape (verse 25), but they ran toward the water as it came back.

decisions.choice: threw
decisions.reason: Readable says "threw" for the picture of shaking off.

records.source: וַיָּשֻׁ֣בוּ הַמַּ֗יִם וַיְכַסּ֤וּ אֶת־הָרֶ֨כֶב֙ וְאֶת־הַפָּ֣רָשִׁ֔ים לְכֹל֙ חֵ֣יל פַּרְעֹ֔ה הַבָּאִ֥ים אַחֲרֵיהֶ֖ם בַּיָּ֑ם לֹֽא־נִשְׁאַ֥ר בָּהֶ֖ם עַד־אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: And returned the waters and covered the chariots and the horsemen, [even] all [the] army of Pharaoh which had gone after them into the sea; not remained among them even one.
pieces: The waters came back and covered the chariots and the horsemen, the whole of Pharaoh's army that had followed Israel into the sea. Not a single one of them was left.

L.28: And the waters returned and covered the chariots and the horsemen, all the army of Pharaoh that had gone in after them into the sea; there did not remain among them even one.

R.28: The water came back and covered the chariots and the horsemen. It covered Pharaoh's whole army that had followed the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} into the sea. Not one of them was left alive.

decisions.choice: all the army of Pharaoh: that is, the whole force that went in
decisions.reason: The phrase sums up the chariots and horsemen: all of Pharaoh's army that followed Israel into the sea.

decisions.choice: not even one remained: as with the flies and the locusts
decisions.reason: The same words were said of the flies (8:27) and the locusts that were swept into the sea (10:19). Now it is said of Pharaoh's army.

decisions.choice: Israel / the Israelites
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "after them"; Balanced and Readable say who they were.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל הָלְכ֥וּ בַיַּבָּשָׁ֖ה בְּת֣וֹךְ הַיָּ֑ם וְהַמַּ֤יִם לָהֶם֙ חֹמָ֔ה מִֽימִינָ֖ם וּמִשְּׂמֹאלָֽם
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Israel walked on dry ground in [the] midst of the sea, and the waters [were] to them a wall on their right and on their left.
pieces: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, though, walked on dry ground through the middle of the sea, with the water a wall for them to the right and to the left.

L.29: But the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel walked on dry ground in the midst of the sea, and the waters [were] a wall to them on their right and on their left.

R.29: But the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} walked through the middle of the sea on dry ground. The water was like a wall on their right and on their left.

decisions.choice: but the sons of Israel walked: a contrast with the Egyptians
decisions.reason: The sentence begins with its subject, setting Israel against the drowned Egyptians of verse 28. It repeats verse 22 as a summary: those who went in after them died; Israel walked through.

records.source: וַיּ֨וֹשַׁע יְהוָ֜ה בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֛וּא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִיַּ֣ד מִצְרָ֑יִם וַיַּ֤רְא יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶת־מִצְרַ֔יִם מֵ֖ת עַל־שְׂפַ֥ת הַיָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And saved Yahweh on that day Israel from [the] hand of Egypt, and saw Israel Egypt dead on [the] shore of the sea.
pieces: So on that day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saved Israel from the power of Egypt, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead along the edge of the sea.

L.30: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saved Israel on that day from the hand of the Egyptians, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the shore of the sea.

R.30: That day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saved Israel from the Egyptians. The Israelites saw the bodies of the Egyptians lying on the seashore.

decisions.choice: saved: rescued, delivered
decisions.reason: The verb is the root of "salvation" in verse 13. What Moses promised has happened.

decisions.choice: from the hand of the Egyptians: from their power
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power and control (3:8; 18:9-10).

decisions.choice: Israel saw the Egyptians dead: Moses' word in verse 13 fulfilled
decisions.reason: Moses said they would never see the Egyptians again. They see them once more, but dead: the threat is over.

decisions.choice: from the power of Egypt (Balanced); from the Egyptians (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "the hand" means; Literal keeps it.

records.source: וַיַּ֨רְא יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶת־הַיָּ֣ד הַגְּדֹלָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם וַיִּֽירְא֥וּ הָעָ֖ם אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּֽאֲמִ֨ינוּ֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה וּבְמֹשֶׁ֖ה עַבְדּֽוֹ׃פ
records.gloss: And saw Israel the hand the great which had done Yahweh against Egypt, and feared the people Yahweh, and they believed in Yahweh and in Moses his servant.
pieces: Israel had seen the great hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at work against Egypt. So the people feared {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they believed in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and in Moses, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant.

L.31: And Israel saw the great hand that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had done against Egypt, and the people feared {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they believed in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and in Moses {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant.

R.31: When the Israelites saw what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had done to Egypt with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great power, they were filled with awe before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They believed in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and in Moses, who served {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: the great hand: the great power and the mighty deed
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power, and here for what that power did. God had promised to bring Israel out with a strong hand (3:19-20; 6:1).

decisions.choice: feared Yahweh: stood in awe of him
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in verse 10, where the people were afraid of the Egyptians. Now their fear is turned to Yahweh: reverence and awe at what he has done.

decisions.choice: they believed in Yahweh and in Moses his servant: the fear of 4:1 answered
decisions.reason: Moses feared the people would not believe him (4:1). They believed at the signs (4:31), lost heart under their labor (6:9), and now believe in Yahweh and in Moses. Moses is called Yahweh's servant again in Numbers 12:7 and Deuteronomy 34:5.

decisions.choice: the great hand of the LORD at work (Balanced); his great power (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of the hand; Readable says what it means.

decisions.choice: were filled with awe before
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "feared" here, which is reverence, not terror. Literal and Balanced keep "feared".
